record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: In the tree T, the size of any minimal subtree of index n is O(log n).

evidence.quote: In the tree T, the size of any minimal subtree of index n is O(log n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma=\{0,1,2\}$ and let $L\subseteq\Sigma^{*}$ be the language of all square-free words over $\Sigma$, i.e. words containing no nonempty factor of the form $uu$. Order $L$ by the prefix relation; the resulting Hasse diagram is an infinite tree $T$ whose root is the empty word and whose children of a node $w\in L$ are the words $wa$ ($a\in\Sigma$) that still belong to $L$. For a node $w\in L$, write $T(w)$ for the subtree of $T$ rooted at $w$, and call $T(w)$ a "minimal subtree of index $n$" if $|w|=n$ and $T(w)$ is finite (equivalently, $w$ has no infinite extension in $L$, while every proper prefix of $w$ does). The size $|T(w)|$ is the number of nodes of $T(w)$.

Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for every $n\ge 1$ and every minimal subtree $T(w)$ of index $n$ in $T$,
$$|T(w)| \;\le\; C\log n.$$
Equivalently, the size of any minimal subtree of index $n$ in $T$ is $O(\log n)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture concerns the tree of ternary square-free words studied by Petrova and Shur (WORDS 2015), who proved that non-branching paths from a node at level $n$ have length $O(\log n)$. The stronger statement that every minimal (finite) subtree at level $n$ has total size $O(\log n)$ is listed among the open problems compiled from the WORDS conferences (1997–2017), and no published resolution was found in the available search results.

status_evidence.title: On the Tree of Ternary Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Non-branching paths in this tree are short: such a path from a node of nth level has length O(log n).
status_evidence.claim: Petrova–Shur establish the O(log n) bound for non-branching paths, the source of the broader conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems and conjectures stated during the ten last meetings WORDS in connection with the development of Combinatorics on Words.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture appears in the WORDS open-problems compilation, indicating it was open at the time of publication.
